room.title: Remote and Hybrid Teams
room.description: How a team spread across Melbourne, Lisbon and Toronto hands work around the clock and decides things in writing — the handover log, the async rituals and the decision log, so nobody has to be awake for the meeting to know what happened.

desks.title: Three-hub handover — enterprise implementations
desks.description: How 11 implementation consultants in Melbourne, Lisbon and Toronto pass live customer work around the clock: the handover log, what a clean handover needs, and today's handover note.
desks.brief:
## Three-hub handover — enterprise implementations

**Team** Implementation · 11 consultants · Melbourne (4), Lisbon (4), Toronto (3)
**Overlap** Lisbon–Toronto about three hours a day; Melbourne–Lisbon and Toronto–Melbourne about an hour each, at the edges of the day
**Live implementations** 9 customers, each with one accountable owner and two hubs covering

### Why handovers matter
A customer's go-live doesn't wait for one hub to wake up. Work moves Melbourne → Lisbon → Toronto → Melbourne, and each move is a written handover on this desk. A poor handover costs a day: the next hub spends its morning asking questions of people who have logged off.

### What we measure
For every handover: items passed, items picked up within the first hour, and questions bounced back. Since the five-heading template went in (@-3d), questions bounced back have fallen from 5–6 per handover to 1–3.

### This week
Harrow Freight goes live @+5d. Its payroll data migration is mid-flight across all three hubs, and the last Toronto → Melbourne handover bounced three questions back — see today's note. Year-to-date amounts move with the migration, so any change of BMS ID or Payroll IDs has to be reported to the ATO, or Harrow's staff see duplicate income statements.

callout.title: Today: Harrow Freight field mapping
callout.body: The last Toronto → Melbourne handover bounced back 3 questions: the payroll field mapping wasn't explained. Inês has the corrected file; it goes into today's Lisbon → Toronto handover. If Toronto can't run the test import overnight, go-live @+5d slips.

The customer's mood, in one line

blocks.h3: Handover — customer — from hub → to hub

blocks.p: Copy this into the day's handover note. Five headings, nothing else. If a heading is empty, write 'nothing' so the next hub knows it wasn't forgotten.

ol: **Your next actions** — one owner each, in priority order
**Waiting on** — customer, another team or a vendor, and since when
**Don't do** — anything that looks obvious but isn't
**Wake me if** — the one situation worth a call

blocks.p: The template went in @-3d. Before it, the receiving hub spent its first hour asking questions of people who had gone to bed. 'Don't do' and 'Wake me if' are the two headings nobody wrote before, and the two that prevent the most rework.
Usually when an attachment changes and the note describes it instead of linking the new version — which is exactly what happened on Harrow Freight @-1d.

desks.title: Async rituals and the team decision log
desks.description: How the team decides in writing across three time zones: proposals, comment windows and decisions in one log, plus the rituals that moved from meetings to writing.
desks.brief:
## Async rituals and the decision log

**Team** Implementation · 11 people, three hubs, no working hour all three share
**Rule** anything that affects more than one hub is decided in writing, here
**Comment window** 48 hours, so every hub gets two working days to see it

### How a decision works
1. The proposer adds a row: the decision, the options and their recommendation
2. It stays **Open for comment** for 48 hours
3. The owner decides, writes one paragraph of why, and marks it **Decided**
4. Reversible decisions can go ahead on fewer comments; irreversible ones need a voice from each hub

### What moved from meetings to writing
The daily stand-up became a written check-in. The weekly team meeting dropped from 60 to 30 minutes and only covers decisions that stalled. Live time per person went from 3h 15m to 1h 30m a week — 1h 45m back each, about 19 hours a week across the 11 of us — and live slots rotate so no hub always takes the 7:00 call.

### Where it stands
12 decisions logged this quarter: 7 decided, 2 open for comment, 2 proposed, 1 being revisited.

callout.title: Closes @+1d: a fourth Toronto consultant
callout.body: Toronto has three consultants and covers the longest overnight leg for both other hubs. The comment window closes @+1d and Melbourne hasn't commented yet. Not reversible, so Grace waits for one voice from each hub.

rows.decision: Daily stand-up becomes a written check-in
Weekly team meeting: 30 min, stalled decisions only
Live meetings rotate across hub time zones
No go-lives on the last working day of any hub's week
Customer kickoff calls recorded for the other hubs
One shared folder structure for customer files
Written check-in format: three fixed lines

children.label: Read the handover before the chat
One voice per hub if irreversible
No DMs to people who are asleep

blocks.h3: Daily stand-up becomes a written check-in

blocks.p: **Owner** Grace · **Logged** @-41d · **Status** Decided; the format is being revisited

The 15-minute stand-up ran at 7:30 in Melbourne, which is 21:30 the night before in Lisbon and the end of the working day in Toronto. Lisbon joined after dinner, Toronto was tired, and half the updates were for people who weren't there.

ul: Keep the live stand-up and rotate the time
Hub-level stand-ups plus a written cross-hub summary
Written check-in only, by 10:00 local time

blocks.p: Written check-in only. Reversible: if a blocker sits unseen for more than a day, a twice-weekly live slot comes back.
Josh: check-ins have crept to 200 words. Proposal: three fixed lines — done, next, blocked — with anything longer moving into the handover note.

notes.title: Comments so far — fourth Toronto hire
notes.body:
- Rafael (Lisbon): yes — Toronto picks up every Lisbon evening problem
- Priyanka (Toronto): yes, but hire for payroll experience, not general implementation
- Sanne (Lisbon): could a Lisbon consultant move to a later day instead?
- Melbourne: no comments yet — Grace to nudge in their morning

Irreversible, so the decision waits for one Melbourne voice.

notes.title: Before weekend on-call opens for comment
notes.body:
Tariq's proposal is irreversible, so settle these before the 48 hours start:

- Melbourne: under Australia's right to disconnect, staff can refuse out-of-hours contact unless refusing is unreasonable, and whether on-call is paid is one of the factors. Rostered and paid, then, not assumed
- Lisbon and Toronto have their own out-of-hours rules. Sanne and Priyanka to check
- Toronto's Friday evening is already Saturday morning in Melbourne. Whose weekend does the rota follow?

stickies.title: Before you propose
stickies.body: Is it reversible? Then decide it, log it, and move on. Don't wait 48 hours.
